facts.note: At nine by the temple bell, everyone showed watches; Félix's watch read twenty minutes to nine and Aurèle scolded him for it.
When the temple struck ten, she looked at the salon clock, which showed five minutes to ten.
She and the doctor (Casimir) played piquet in the salon without a break until he went out for cigars at twenty-eight minutes past ten by the salon clock.
As he left he asked her to play; she sat at the piano at once, played until he returned, and stopped when he came in.
A moment after his return, the hall clock struck eleven.

added.quote: I remember that, because it struck the hour before Casimir had finished telling me about the damp.
added.why: Places the end of Casimir's remark about the damp cigars after the hall clock struck eleven, so Casimir was still in the room with her at eleven. This is a whereabouts and an order the sheet does not give.
